exercises.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.description: A foundational pressing movement that builds strength and size across the front and side deltoids while engaging the triceps.
instructions: Stand or sit with your feet shoulder-width apart and a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Brace your core and keep your ribcage down to protect your lower back.
Press both dumbbells straight overhead until your arms are nearly locked out, without shrugging your shoulders up.
Pause briefly at the top with the weights stacked over your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells under control back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, keeping the motion smooth and avoiding leaning back.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.description: An isolation exercise that targets the side deltoids to build shoulder width and definition.
instructions: Stand tall holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and brace your core.
Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach roughly shoulder height.
Lead with your elbows rather than your hands and avoid shrugging.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower slowly under control.
Repeat, using a weight light enough to maintain strict form.

exercises.name: Front Raise
exercises.description: Isolates the front deltoids to improve pressing strength and shoulder aesthetics.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
Keep your elbows slightly bent and your core braced.
Raise one or both arms straight in front of you to about shoulder height.
Avoid swinging or using momentum from your hips.
Pause at the top, then lower the weight slowly.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, keeping your torso still.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Reverse Fly
exercises.description: Targets the rear deltoids and upper back to balance shoulder development and improve posture.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Let the dumbbells hang beneath your shoulders with a slight bend in your elbows.
Keep your back flat and your neck neutral.
Raise both arms out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Stop when your arms reach shoulder level, avoiding a shrug.
Lower the weights slowly and repeat.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight movement that shifts load onto the shoulders to build pressing strength without equipment.
instructions: Start in a push-up position, then walk your feet toward your hands to form an inverted V shape.
Position your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width with hips high.
Bend your elbows to lower the crown of your head toward the floor.
Keep your core tight and your back straight throughout.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
Repeat, keeping the movement controlled to protect your neck.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: The classic compound press for building overall chest strength and mass, also engaging the shoulders and triceps.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor and eyes under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack it over your chest.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest, keeping your elbows at roughly 45 degrees.
Keep your shoulder blades retracted and a slight arch in your lower back.
Press the bar back up until your arms are extended without locking harshly.
Use a spotter for heavier sets and keep the bar path smooth.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.description: A versatile bodyweight exercise that builds chest, shoulder, and triceps strength anywhere.
instructions: Start in a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and body in a straight line.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips level.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Keep your elbows tucked at about 45 degrees from your torso.
Press back up until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat, avoiding sagging hips or flaring elbows.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.description: Emphasizes the upper chest for balanced development while allowing a natural range of motion.
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 30 to 45 degree incline and sit back with a dumbbell in each hand.
Start with the dumbbells at the sides of your upper chest, palms facing forward.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and your feet flat on the floor.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly together until your arms are extended.
Lower them slowly to the starting position with control.
Repeat, maintaining tension in your chest throughout.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
exercises.description: An isolation movement that stretches and contracts the chest for improved size and definition.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, palms facing each other.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows that stays fixed throughout the movement.
Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Stop before your elbows drop below the bench to protect your shoulders.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together over your chest.
Repeat with slow, controlled motion and a light-to-moderate weight.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
exercises.description: A beginner-friendly push-up variation that reduces load and helps build pressing strength progressively.
instructions: Place your hands on a sturdy elevated surface such as a bench or box, slightly wider than shoulders.
Step your feet back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and keep your neck neutral.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the surface.
Press back up until your arms are extended.
Repeat, lowering the surface height over time to increase difficulty.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
exercises.description: A staple isolation exercise for building biceps size and arm strength.
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso and your core braced.
Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders by bending at the elbows.
Avoid swinging your body or letting your elbows drift forward.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower slowly under control.
Repeat for the prescribed reps with a smooth tempo.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.description: Targets the biceps and brachialis with a neutral grip to build arm thickness and grip strength.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing your body (neutral grip).
Keep your elbows pinned at your sides and your shoulders relaxed.
Curl the dumbbells up while keeping your palms facing inward the whole time.
Raise until the weights approach your shoulders without swinging.
Pause and squeeze, then lower slowly to the start.
Repeat, maintaining a controlled tempo throughout.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.description: A heavy compound curl that allows progressive overload for maximum biceps growth.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a barbell with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your core braced.
Curl the bar up toward your chest by flexing your biceps.
Avoid using momentum or leaning back to lift the weight.
Squeeze at the top, then lower the bar slowly to full extension.
Repeat for the prescribed reps with strict form.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.description: An isolation curl that maximizes biceps peak contraction by removing momentum.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs spread and lean slightly forward.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and brace that elbow against the inside of your thigh.
Let the arm hang extended with your palm facing away.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder, keeping your upper arm still.
Squeeze hard at the top of the movement.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch arms.

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.description: A bodyweight pull that heavily recruits the biceps while also building back strength.
instructions: Grab a pull-up bar with an underhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms extended and your core engaged.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down until your chin clears the bar.
Keep your shoulders down and avoid swinging.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower yourself with control.
Repeat, using an assistance band if needed to complete the reps.

exercises.name: Wrist Curl
exercises.description: Isolates the forearm flexors to build grip and wrist strength.
instructions: Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists just past your knees, palms up.
Hold a light dumbbell or barbell with your hands hanging off the edge.
Let the weight roll toward your fingertips as you lower it.
Curl your wrists upward by flexing your forearms.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.
Repeat for higher reps to build endurance and strength.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl
exercises.description: Strengthens the forearm extensors to balance grip development and support wrist health.
instructions: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs with your wrists past your knees, palms facing down.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand with your knuckles pointing toward the floor.
Lower the weight by letting your wrists drop under control.
Raise your knuckles upward by extending your wrists.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
Use a light weight to maintain strict form and avoid strain.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.description: A loaded carry that builds tremendous grip strength, forearm endurance, and full-body stability.
instructions: Stand between two heavy dumbbells or kettlebells and grip one in each hand.
Stand tall with your shoulders back and your core braced.
Walk forward with controlled steps, keeping your posture upright.
Grip the weights firmly and avoid letting your shoulders slump.
Continue for the prescribed distance or time.
Set the weights down under control and rest between rounds.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl
exercises.description: Works the forearm extensors and brachialis using an overhand grip for thicker, stronger arms.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell or dumbbells with an overhand grip at thigh level.
Keep your elbows tucked at your sides and your core engaged.
Curl the weight up toward your chest while keeping your palms facing down.
Avoid swinging or using momentum.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly under control.
Repeat with a lighter weight than a standard curl.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.description: A simple hang that builds grip endurance, forearm strength, and shoulder stability.
instructions: Grab a pull-up bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart.
Let your body hang fully with your arms extended.
Engage your shoulders slightly rather than hanging completely loose.
Keep your core lightly braced and your body still.
Hold the position for as long as you can maintain a solid grip.
Drop down safely and rest before repeating.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description: An isometric hold that builds deep core stability and endurance throughout the abdominals.
instructions: Start face down and prop yourself onto your forearms and toes.
Position your elbows directly under your shoulders.
Form a straight line from your head to your heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to prevent your hips from sagging.
Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor just ahead of you.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, breathing steadily.

exercises.name: Crunch
exercises.description: A classic movement that targets the upper abdominals with a short, controlled range of motion.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your hands lightly behind your head or across your chest.
Brace your core and tuck your chin slightly.
Curl your shoulders off the floor by contracting your abs.
Avoid pulling on your neck or using momentum.
Lower slowly to the start and repeat.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description: An advanced exercise that strongly targets the lower abs and hip flexors.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and arms extended.
Engage your shoulders and brace your core.
Raise your legs together by flexing your abs and hips.
Lift until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or higher.
Avoid swinging by controlling the movement.
Lower your legs slowly and repeat.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.description: A dynamic move that works the abs and obliques through rotation and controlled leg motion.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your head and legs lifted, knees bent.
Brace your core and lift your shoulders off the floor.
Bring one knee toward your chest while extending the opposite leg.
Rotate your torso to bring the opposite elbow toward the bent knee.
Alternate sides in a smooth pedaling motion.
Keep your lower back pressed to the floor throughout.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: A core stability exercise that trains the abs to resist movement while protecting the lower back.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms extended toward the ceiling and knees bent at 90 degrees.
Press your lower back gently into the floor and brace your core.
Slowly lower one arm overhead while extending the opposite leg toward the floor.
Stop before your lower back arches off the ground.
Return to the start under control, then switch sides.
Move slowly and breathe steadily throughout.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.description: A rotational core exercise that targets the obliques and improves trunk strength.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet lifted or lightly touching the ground.
Lean back slightly to form a V shape with your torso and thighs.
Hold your hands together or grip a weight in front of your chest.
Brace your core and rotate your torso to one side.
Rotate to the opposite side in a controlled motion.
Continue alternating, keeping your chest lifted and back straight.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description: An isometric hold that builds lateral core stability and strengthens the obliques.
instructions: Lie on your side and prop yourself up on your forearm with your elbow under your shoulder.
Stack your feet and lift your hips off the floor.
Form a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and avoid letting your hips drop.
Hold the position for the prescribed time.
Lower down, then repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.description: A dynamic movement that engages the obliques through torso rotation and cross-body motion.
instructions: Lie on your back with hands lightly behind your head and legs raised, knees bent.
Lift your shoulders off the floor and brace your core.
Bring one knee toward your chest while extending the other leg.
Twist your torso to bring the opposite elbow toward the bent knee.
Alternate sides smoothly without pulling on your neck.
Keep your lower back pressed to the floor throughout.

exercises.name: Standing Side Bend
exercises.description: A simple weighted movement that isolates the obliques through lateral flexion.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Keep your core braced and your shoulders level.
Bend sideways at the waist, lowering the dumbbell toward your knee.
Avoid leaning forward or backward as you bend.
Contract your obliques to return to an upright position.
Complete the reps, then switch to the other side.

exercises.name: Woodchopper
exercises.description: A cross-body rotational exercise that builds functional oblique strength and power.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a dumbbell or medicine ball with both hands.
Start with the weight raised above one shoulder.
Brace your core and rotate your torso as you pull the weight diagonally across your body.
Finish with the weight near your opposite hip, pivoting your back foot.
Control the movement back to the starting position.
Complete the reps, then switch directions.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.description: The king of lower-body exercises, building powerful quads, glutes, and overall leg strength.
instructions: Position a barbell across your upper back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Keep your back neutral throughout and use a rack for safety.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.description: A foundational movement that builds leg strength and mobility with no equipment.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.
Extend your arms in front of you for balance and brace your core.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower down.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor or as low as comfortable.
Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
exercises.description: A dynamic single-leg exercise that builds quad strength, balance, and coordination.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet together and hands on your hips or holding dumbbells.
Step forward with one leg into a long stride.
Lower your body until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and your torso upright.
Push through your front heel to step forward into the next lunge.
Continue alternating legs for the prescribed reps.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.description: A machine-based exercise that lets you load the quads heavily with reduced spinal stress.
instructions: Sit in the leg press machine with your back flat against the pad.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Release the safety and lower the platform by bending your knees.
Descend until your knees reach about 90 degrees without your lower back rounding.
Press the platform back up through your heels without locking your knees harshly.
Repeat for the prescribed reps with controlled tempo.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.description: A challenging single-leg exercise that builds quad strength, stability, and balance.
instructions: Stand a couple of feet in front of a bench and place the top of one foot on it behind you.
Keep your torso upright and your core braced.
Lower your body by bending your front knee until your thigh is near parallel.
Keep your front knee tracking over your foot.
Drive through your front heel to return to the start.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Leg Raise
exercises.description: An isolation exercise that strengthens the outer hip abductors and improves hip stability.
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs stacked and straight.
Support your head with your lower arm and place your top hand on the floor for balance.
Brace your core to keep your torso stable.
Raise your top leg upward while keeping it straight.
Lift until you feel your outer hip engage, then pause.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Banded Lateral Walk
exercises.description: A resistance-band exercise that activates the hip abductors and glute medius for stability.
instructions: Place a resistance band around your legs just above your knees or ankles.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and a slight bend in your knees, in a quarter-squat.
Keep your core braced and your chest up.
Step sideways with one foot, maintaining tension in the band.
Follow with the other foot without letting your knees cave in.
Continue stepping for the prescribed reps, then reverse direction.

exercises.name: Clamshell
exercises.description: A targeted movement that activates the glute medius and hip abductors to support the hips and knees.
instructions: Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent at about 45 degrees, legs stacked.
Rest your head on your lower arm and keep your feet together.
Brace your core and keep your hips stacked without rolling back.
Open your top knee upward like a clamshell while keeping your feet touching.
Pause at the top and squeeze your glute.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Cable Hip Abduction
exercises.description: A cable exercise that isolates the abductors under constant tension for stronger, more stable hips.
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable and secure it around your outer ankle.
Stand side-on to the machine and hold the frame for balance.
Brace your core and keep your torso upright.
Lift the working leg out to the side against the cable resistance.
Pause at the top, then return slowly under control.
Complete all reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: Standing Banded Abduction
exercises.description: A standing movement that builds abductor strength and single-leg balance.
instructions: Loop a resistance band around both ankles and stand tall.
Hold onto a wall or sturdy surface for balance if needed.
Shift your weight onto one leg and brace your core.
Lift the other leg out to the side against the band's resistance.
Keep your leg straight and your torso upright, avoiding leaning.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch legs.

exercises.name: Sumo Squat
exercises.description: A wide-stance squat that emphasizes the inner thighs and adductors along with the glutes.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width and toes turned out.
Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell at your chest or between your legs.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat.
Descend until your thighs are parallel, keeping your knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your heels and inner thighs to stand back up.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Inner Thigh Raise
exercises.description: An isolation move that directly targets the adductor muscles of the inner thigh.
instructions: Lie on your side with your bottom leg straight and your top leg bent and crossed in front.
Support your head with your lower arm and place your top hand on the floor.
Brace your core to stabilize your torso.
Lift your bottom, straight leg upward toward the ceiling.
Raise until you feel your inner thigh contract, then pause.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
exercises.description: A lateral squat that stretches and strengthens the adductors while improving hip mobility.
instructions: Stand with your feet in a wide stance, wider than shoulder-width.
Shift your weight to one side, bending that knee while keeping the other leg straight.
Lower down as far as your mobility allows, keeping the heel of the bent leg down.
Keep your chest up and the straightened leg's toes pointing up.
Push back to center through the bent leg.
Repeat on the other side, alternating throughout.

exercises.name: Cable Hip Adduction
exercises.description: A cable exercise that isolates the inner thigh under constant tension for targeted strength.
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable and secure it around your inner ankle.
Stand side-on with the working leg closest to the machine.
Hold the frame for balance and brace your core.
Pull the working leg across your body toward your midline against the resistance.
Pause at the point of full contraction.
Return slowly and repeat, then switch legs.

exercises.name: Adductor Squeeze
exercises.description: An isometric exercise that activates and strengthens the adductors using a ball or cushion.
instructions: Lie on your back or sit with your knees bent and a small ball or cushion between your knees.
Brace your core and keep your spine neutral.
Squeeze your knees together against the ball as hard as is comfortable.
Hold the squeeze while breathing steadily.
Maintain tension for the prescribed time.
Release slowly and repeat for the prescribed rounds.

exercises.name: Steady-State Running
exercises.description: A sustained-pace run that builds aerobic endurance and cardiovascular health.
instructions: Begin with a 5-minute brisk walk or light jog to warm up.
Settle into a conversational pace where you can still speak in short sentences.
Keep your posture tall, shoulders relaxed, and arms swinging naturally.
Land midfoot and maintain a steady breathing rhythm.
Hold the pace for the target duration.
Finish with a 5-minute cooldown walk and light stretching.

exercises.name: High-Intensity Interval Training
exercises.description: Alternating bursts of intense effort and recovery to boost conditioning and burn calories efficiently.
instructions: Warm up for 5 minutes with light cardio and dynamic movements.
Perform 20 to 30 seconds of all-out effort such as sprinting or fast cycling.
Follow with 40 to 60 seconds of easy-paced active recovery.
Repeat the work-and-recovery cycle for the target number of rounds.
Keep your form sharp even as fatigue sets in.
Cool down for 5 minutes with easy movement to lower your heart rate.

exercises.name: Jump Rope
exercises.description: A rhythmic full-body cardio exercise that improves coordination, footwork, and endurance.
instructions: Hold the rope handles with the rope resting behind your heels.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and turn the rope with your wrists.
Jump just high enough to clear the rope, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Maintain a steady rhythm and keep your core engaged.
Start with short intervals and build up your continuous time.
Rest as needed and cool down when finished.

exercises.name: Cycling
exercises.description: A low-impact cardio workout that builds leg endurance and cardiovascular fitness.
instructions: Adjust the seat so your knee has a slight bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Warm up with 5 minutes of easy pedaling.
Settle into a moderate, sustainable resistance and cadence.
Keep your core engaged and your grip relaxed on the handlebars.
Maintain steady effort for the target duration, or add intervals to increase intensity.
Cool down with 5 minutes of easy pedaling.

exercises.name: Rowing Machine
exercises.description: A full-body cardio and strength workout that engages the legs, back, and arms.
instructions: Strap your feet in and grip the handle with your arms extended.
Begin the drive by pushing through your legs first.
Once your legs are nearly straight, lean back slightly and pull the handle to your lower ribs.
Reverse the sequence: extend your arms, hinge forward, then bend your knees.
Keep a smooth, controlled rhythm and avoid rounding your back.
Continue for the target duration, maintaining consistent strokes.

exercises.name: Triceps Dip
exercises.description: A bodyweight pressing movement that builds triceps strength and mass.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a sturdy bench and place your hands next to your hips, fingers forward.
Slide your hips off the bench with your legs extended or knees bent.
Keep your shoulders down and your chest up.
Bend your elbows to lower your body until they reach about 90 degrees.
Keep your elbows pointing straight back, not flaring out.
Press through your palms to return to the start and repeat.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.description: An isolation exercise that targets the long head of the triceps through a full stretch.
instructions: Stand or sit holding a single dumbbell with both hands overhead.
Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your head.
Brace your core and keep your ribcage down.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms back to the top by contracting your triceps.
Repeat with a controlled tempo, keeping your upper arms still.

exercises.name: Triceps Rope Pushdown
exercises.description: A cable exercise that isolates the triceps with constant tension for strength and definition.
instructions: Attach a rope to a high cable and grip an end in each hand.
Stand tall with your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Brace your core and keep a slight forward lean.
Push the rope down by extending your elbows until your arms are straight.
Spread the rope apart slightly at the bottom for a full contraction.
Return slowly to the start, keeping your elbows pinned.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up variation that shifts emphasis onto the triceps.
instructions: Start in a plank with your hands close together beneath your chest.
Keep your body in a straight line and your core braced.
Lower your chest toward your hands by bending your elbows.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your body throughout.
Press back up until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat, avoiding sagging hips or flaring elbows.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.description: A lying triceps extension that effectively isolates and builds the triceps.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a barbell or dumbbells with arms extended over your chest.
Keep your upper arms vertical and your elbows pointing toward the ceiling.
Bend your elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead.
Stop just above your forehead, keeping your upper arms still.
Extend your elbows to press the weight back to the start.
Use a controlled tempo and a manageable weight to protect your elbows.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.description: A direct trap exercise that builds upper-back and neck strength and size.
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your body.
Keep your arms straight and your core braced.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Avoid rolling your shoulders forward or backward.
Pause and squeeze at the top of the movement.
Lower slowly under control and repeat.

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug
exercises.description: A heavy shrug variation that allows progressive overload for maximum trap development.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip at thigh level, hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your arms straight, chest up, and core engaged.
Shrug your shoulders straight up as high as possible.
Avoid using your arms or rolling your shoulders.
Pause at the top, then lower the bar slowly.
Repeat for the prescribed reps with controlled motion.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.description: A cable exercise that strengthens the mid-traps and rear delts to improve posture and shoulder health.
instructions: Attach a rope to a cable set at about face height.
Grip an end in each hand with your palms facing inward and step back to create tension.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Pull the rope toward your face, driving your elbows out and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.
Return slowly to the start and repeat.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
exercises.description: A loaded carry that builds trap endurance, grip strength, and overall stability.
instructions: Grip a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
Stand tall with your shoulders pulled back and down.
Brace your core and keep your traps engaged to support the load.
Walk forward with controlled, steady steps.
Maintain upright posture without letting your shoulders slump.
Continue for the prescribed distance, then set the weights down safely.

exercises.name: Prone Y Raise
exercises.description: A bodyweight movement that strengthens the lower traps to improve shoulder positioning and posture.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor or an incline bench with your arms extended overhead in a Y shape.
Keep your thumbs pointing up toward the ceiling.
Brace your core and keep your neck neutral.
Raise your arms off the floor by squeezing your lower traps and shoulder blades.
Lift until you feel your upper back engage, avoiding shrugging.
Lower slowly and repeat with control.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.description: A challenging bodyweight pull that builds a wide, strong back and powerful lats.
instructions: Grab a pull-up bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Hang with your arms extended and your core engaged.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down and back.
Continue until your chin clears the bar.
Keep your shoulders down and avoid swinging.
Lower yourself slowly to full extension and repeat.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: A cable exercise that mimics the pull-up and effectively targets the lats with adjustable resistance.
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown machine and secure your thighs under the pads.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width.
Lean back slightly and keep your chest up.
Pull the bar down toward your upper chest by driving your elbows down.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom.
Return the bar slowly to the top without shrugging, and repeat.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Barbell Row
exercises.description: A compound pulling movement that builds thickness across the lats and mid-back.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with an overhand grip, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at your hips until your torso is at about 45 degrees, keeping your back flat.
Let the bar hang with your arms extended.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the bar slowly under control and repeat.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: A unilateral row that targets each lat individually to correct imbalances and build back strength.
instructions: Place one knee and hand on a bench with your other foot on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in your free hand with your arm extended.
Keep your back flat and parallel to the floor.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip by driving your elbow back.
Squeeze your lat at the top without rotating your torso.
Lower slowly and repeat, then switch sides.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.description: An isolation exercise that targets the lats without significant arm involvement.
instructions: Stand facing a high cable with a straight bar attached.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip and step back slightly.
Keep your arms straight with a soft bend in your elbows.
Pull the bar down toward your thighs in an arc using your lats.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom of the movement.
Return slowly to the start, keeping your core braced.

exercises.name: Superman
exercises.description: A bodyweight exercise that strengthens the lower back and improves spinal stability.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor.
Brace your core lightly to protect your spine.
Raise your arms, chest, and legs off the floor simultaneously.
Squeeze your lower back and glutes at the top.
Lower slowly under control and repeat.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: A core and lower-back stability exercise that trains balanced, controlled movement.
instructions: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Brace your core and keep your spine neutral.
Extend one arm forward while extending the opposite leg back.
Keep your hips level and avoid arching your lower back.
Pause when your arm and leg are in line with your torso.
Return under control, then repeat on the other side.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hip-hinge movement that builds the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings while teaching proper hinging.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell or dumbbells in front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and your chest up.
Push your hips back to lower the weight along your legs.
Keep your back flat and the weight close to your body.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, then drive your hips forward to stand.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and avoid rounding your back.

exercises.name: Back Extension
exercises.description: An isolation exercise that directly strengthens the erector spinae of the lower back.
instructions: Position yourself on a back extension bench with your hips on the pad and feet secured.
Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands behind your head.
Keep your spine neutral and hinge forward at the hips.
Lower your torso until you feel a stretch, keeping your back flat.
Raise your torso by contracting your lower back and glutes until your body is straight.
Avoid over-extending at the top, and repeat with control.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: A foundational movement that strengthens the posterior chain and supports lower-back health.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Rest your arms at your sides and brace your core.
Press through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, forming a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Avoid overarching your lower back at the top.
Lower slowly under control and repeat.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.description: A premier glute-building exercise that allows heavy loading for strength and size.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and a barbell or weight across your hips.
Bend your knees and place your feet flat, shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core and tuck your chin slightly.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top without overarching your back.
Lower slowly under control and repeat.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: A bodyweight movement that activates and strengthens the glutes with no equipment needed.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Place your arms at your sides and brace your core.
Press through your heels to raise your hips toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, forming a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Avoid arching your lower back excessively.
Lower slowly and repeat for the prescribed reps.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hip-hinge exercise that heavily targets the glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell or dumbbells in front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart.
Keep a soft bend in your knees and your chest up.
Hinge at your hips, pushing them back to lower the weight along your legs.
Keep your back flat and the weight close to your body.
Lower until you feel a hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and repeat.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: A single-leg exercise that emphasizes the glutes while building balance and stability.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips or holding dumbbells.
Step one foot back into a long stride.
Lower your body until both knees are bent at about 90 degrees.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and your torso upright.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Repeat, alternating legs or completing all reps on one side first.

exercises.name: Cable Kickback
exercises.description: An isolation exercise that targets each glute individually under constant tension.
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable and secure it around one ankle.
Face the machine and hold the frame for balance.
Brace your core and keep a slight bend in your standing knee.
Kick the working leg straight back by squeezing your glute.
Pause at the top without arching your lower back.
Return slowly under control and repeat, then switch legs.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: A hip-hinge movement that provides a deep hamstring stretch and builds posterior-chain strength.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell or dumbbells in front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart.
Keep a slight bend in your knees throughout the movement.
Push your hips back to lower the weight down the front of your legs.
Keep your back flat and the weight close to your body.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing and squeeze your glutes.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.description: A machine exercise that isolates the hamstrings through knee flexion.
instructions: Lie face down on a leg curl machine with the pad resting just above your heels.
Grip the handles and keep your hips pressed into the bench.
Brace your core to prevent your lower back from arching.
Curl the pad toward your glutes by bending your knees.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top of the movement.
Lower slowly under control and repeat.

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
exercises.description: An advanced eccentric exercise that dramatically strengthens the hamstrings and aids injury prevention.
instructions: Kneel on a soft pad with your ankles anchored under a secure surface or held by a partner.
Keep your body straight from your knees to your head.
Brace your core and engage your hamstrings and glutes.
Lower your torso toward the floor as slowly as you can control.
Catch yourself with your hands when you can no longer resist.
Push back up and use your hamstrings to return to the start.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Deadlift
exercises.description: A unilateral hinge that builds hamstring strength, balance, and hip stability.
instructions: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
Keep a slight bend in your standing knee.
Hinge at your hips, lowering the weight while extending your free leg behind you.
Keep your back flat and your hips square to the floor.
Lower until you feel a hamstring stretch, then return to standing.
Squeeze your glute at the top, then switch legs.

exercises.name: Glute-Ham Raise
exercises.description: A bodyweight exercise that strengthens the hamstrings and glutes through both hip and knee action.
instructions: Position yourself on a glute-ham developer with your feet anchored and thighs on the pad.
Start with your body straight and horizontal.
Brace your core and engage your hamstrings.
Lower your torso forward by extending at the knees under control.
Curl your body back up by contracting your hamstrings and glutes.
Keep the movement smooth and avoid using momentum.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.description: A fundamental exercise that targets the gastrocnemius to build calf size and strength.
instructions: Stand with the balls of your feet on the edge of a step or raised surface.
Let your heels drop below the level of the step for a full stretch.
Hold onto a wall or rail for balance and brace your core.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels as high as possible.
Squeeze your calves at the top of the movement.
Lower slowly under control and repeat.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.description: A seated variation that emphasizes the soleus muscle deep in the lower leg.
instructions: Sit on a seated calf raise machine or a bench with a weight resting on your thighs.
Place the balls of your feet on the platform with your heels hanging off.
Let your heels drop to feel a stretch in your calves.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.
Repeat with a controlled tempo for a full range of motion.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description: A unilateral raise that builds calf strength and corrects side-to-side imbalances.
instructions: Stand on one foot with the ball of that foot on the edge of a step.
Hold a wall or rail for balance and let your heel drop for a stretch.
Brace your core and keep your standing leg slightly bent.
Press through the ball of your foot to raise your heel as high as possible.
Pause and squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly, complete the reps, then switch legs.

exercises.name: Jump Rope
exercises.description: A dynamic exercise that builds calf endurance and power through repeated bounding.
instructions: Hold the rope handles with the rope behind your heels.
Turn the rope with your wrists while keeping your elbows close.
Jump lightly on the balls of your feet, clearing the rope each turn.
Stay springy through your ankles and calves.
Maintain a steady rhythm for the target time.
Rest as needed and repeat for the prescribed rounds.

exercises.name: Farmer's Walk on Toes
exercises.description: A loaded carry performed on the balls of the feet to build calf strength and endurance.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Rise onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels off the ground.
Brace your core and keep your posture tall.
Walk forward with small, controlled steps while staying on your toes.
Keep your heels elevated throughout the walk.
Continue for the target distance, then lower down and rest.
